title: Lanternfall Ep. 4: The Letter in the Crate (Ada's Logbook, Blind Playthrough)
description: Episode 4 of my blind, in-character playthrough of Lanternfall. Ada finds a letter in a washed-up crate that might change everything about the lamp. Suggest a reason for Ada to enter the chapel in the comments.

content.authorization_basis: Original synthetic transcript authored for the AI Video Discovery project. No real video exists.

segments.text: Day four on Gull Rock. Welcome back to Lanternfall, where I'm playing as Ada Wren,
temporary keeper of a lighthouse on an island that sinks a little bit every night.
For this series I'm doing something slightly different.
I'm keeping Ada's logbook as we go, in character, and I'm only allowed to know what Ada knows.
So no wikis, no guides. If she gets it wrong, I get it wrong.
Last episode ended with the tide eating the vegetable garden, so let's open the logbook.
Entry. Water reached the third fence post overnight. Lost the potatoes.
Kept the seeds in my coat, which is the only smart thing I did all week.
Okay.
Mechanically, what's happening here is the game raises the sea a notch every in-game night, and anything below the line is gone.
So the whole island is basically a countdown timer you can see.
And I love that, because it means every object on this map has a little story about when it's going to drown.
Look at the chapel down there. It's already half underwater.
I've decided Ada refuses to go inside it, because in her head that's where the previous keeper went and didn't come back.
The game never says that, by the way.
I made that up in episode one and now I'm stuck with it. Right, the lamp.
The lamp needs oil every night, and oil comes from the wrecks that wash up.
Here's a crate. Let's see. Oil, two flasks, and a letter. Oh. Oh, this is good.
It's addressed to someone called Brannoch, and it says, the rock is not sinking, the sea is rising,
and the light is the reason. Hmm.
So, as Ada, I'm going to read this as the ravings of a sailor.
As a player, I'm a little bit nervous,
because I think the game just told me that keeping the lamp lit is what's drowning the island.
Which would make the whole thing a dilemma. Light the lamp, ships stay safe, island sinks.
Let the lamp go dark, island survives, ships wreck. And the wrecks are where the oil comes from.
That is a beautiful little loop, if it's true. Let me write that down.
Entry. Found a letter from a madman. Lit the lamp anyway. Ships are people.
Islands are rocks. Let's climb up. The climb is the best bit of this game for me.
Every night the stairs are a little bit wetter at the bottom, and the sound design shifts,
the waves get louder in the stairwell. They don't tell you any of this, you just feel it.
Lamp's lit. And there it is, a ship turning away from the reef. That's twelve ships saved now.
I'm keeping a tally on the wall, which is a thing the game actually lets you do,
you can scratch marks with the knife.
Twelve marks, four days, and the island is about two thirds of the size it was.
I'm going to stop here, because next episode I want to finally go into the chapel,
and I think Ada needs a good reason to break her own rule.
If you've got a reason she'd believe, put it in the comments, and I'll pick one and play it straight.
Last entry for tonight. Twelve ships. Garden gone. The sea is louder than it was.
I am not afraid of the chapel. I'm just busy. Goodnight.
